medications.purpose: Current therapy to lower blood pressure
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends a CCB as part of first‑line therapy for hypertension in adults (especially as component of combination therapy)​

medications.dose: 2.5 mg once daily, increase to 5 mg after 2 weeks if tolerated, target 10 mg once daily
medications.purpose: Add ACE‑I to achieve BP target <140/90 mmHg and provide renal/cardiovascular protection
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136: ACE‑I is first‑line for patients <55 years without contraindication​

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood pressure lowering; risk of symptomatic hypotension, especially after ramipril dose escalation
interactions_checked.action: Start ramipril at low dose, monitor BP and symptoms, advise patient to rise slowly after standing

contraindications.reason: ACE‑Is are teratogenic and contraindicated in pregnancy
contraindications.alternative: If pregnancy confirmed, switch to labetalol or methyldopa per NICE NG136

contraindications.reason: NSAIDs can blunt antihypertensive effect and increase risk of acute kidney injury
contraindications.alternative: Advise patient to avoid regular NSAIDs; use acetaminophen or topical agents for sinusitis pain

Liver function tests not available – required before any future statin initiation

treatment_summary: The patient is on low‑dose amlodipine alone. Per NICE NG136, add ramipril 2.5 mg daily (titrating to 10 mg) as first‑line ACE‑I to achieve BP <140/90 mmHg and provide organ protection. Monitor BP, renal function and potassium after dose changes and then annually. Continue amlodipine. Review in 2–4 weeks; if target BP not reached, consider adding low‑dose indapamide. Address lifestyle (weight loss, diet, exercise) and obtain missing labs (eGFR, electrolytes, lipids, HbA1c, QRISK) before considering statin therapy.
